nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$, each empty or holding an item, and item count $n \le m$. The contents of $T$ is the array obtained from the prefix $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1}$ by skipping the empty slots and keeping the items of the occupied ones, in order.
nodes.title: Formula for the contents of a dynamic table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$, each empty or holding an item, and item count $n \le m$. The contents of $T$ is the array of the items held by the occupied slots among $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1}$, in order; empty slots in this prefix are skipped.
nodes.title: Contents of a dynamic table

nodes.summary: The empty dynamic table has an empty slot array, so capacity $0$, and item count $0$.
nodes.title: The empty dynamic table has no slots and no items

nodes.summary: The empty dynamic table is the table with no slots (capacity $0$) and item count $0$. It models a table before its first allocation.
nodes.title: Empty dynamic table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with item count $n$, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. After applying deletion to $T$, the lookup at logical position $n - 1$ returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup at the vacated position after deletion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table holding $n$ items, and let $i$ be a natural number with $i < n - 1$. After applying deletion to $T$, the lookup at logical position $i$ returns the same result as the lookup at position $i$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Deletion preserves lookups below the last position

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with item count $n$. For every natural number $i \ge n$, the lookup at logical position $i$ in $T$ returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup beyond the item count returns nothing

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table holding $n$ items. For every natural number $i$, the lookup at logical position $i$ in $T$ returns a value if and only if $i < n$.
nodes.title: Lookup succeeds exactly below the item count

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$, each empty or holding an item, and item count $n \le m$. The lookup at logical position $i$ returns the item held by $s_i$ when $i < n$ and $s_i$ is occupied; it returns no value when $i < n$ and $s_i$ is empty, and when $i \ge n$.
nodes.title: Lookup in a dynamic table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table. The contents of the table obtained by applying deletion to $T$ is the contents of $T$ with its last entry removed; when the contents of $T$ is empty, it stays empty.
nodes.title: Deletion removes the last item from the contents

nodes.summary: Applying deletion to a dynamic table with item count $n$ gives a table with item count $n - 1$ when $n \ge 1$, and item count $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Item count after deletion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with capacity $m$ and item count $n$, and apply deletion to $T$. If $n = 0$, the capacity stays $m$. If $n \ge 1$ and $4(n-1) < m$, the new capacity is $\lfloor m/2 \rfloor$. Otherwise the capacity stays $m$.
nodes.title: Capacity after deletion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$ holding $n \ge 1$ items, and let $m'$ be the capacity of the table obtained by applying deletion to $T$. The slots of that table are the first $n - 1$ slots $s_0, \dots, s_{n-2}$ of $T$ followed by $m' - (n - 1)$ empty slots.
nodes.title: Slots after deletion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table, that is, its occupied slots are exactly its first $n$ slots, where $n$ is its item count. Then the table obtained by applying deletion to $T$ is again well-formed.
nodes.title: Deletion preserves well-formedness

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$, each empty or holding an item, and item count $n \le m$. Deleting the last item of $T$ gives the following table. If $n = 0$, the result is $T$ itself. Otherwise, if $4(n-1) < m$, that is, the load factor after deletion is strictly below $1/4$, the table contracts: the result has slots $s_0, \dots, s_{n-2}$ followed by $\lfloor m/2 \rfloor - (n-1)$ empty…
nodes.title: Deletion from a dynamic table

nodes.summary: For a dynamic table $T$ with item count $n$ and capacity (number of slots) $m$, let $\Phi(T) = 2n - m$, an integer that may be negative. If inserting an item $x$ into $T$ has cost $c$ and returns the table $T'$, then $c + \Phi(T') - \Phi(T) \le 3$. Here the cost of an insertion is one unit for writing $x$ plus one unit for each old slot copied when a full table is doubled.
nodes.title: Amortized cost of dynamic-table insertion

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a well-formed dynamic table and $x$ is an item, then the contents of the table obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ are the contents of $T$ followed by $x$.
nodes.title: Insertion appends to the contents

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a well-formed dynamic table and $x_1, \dots, x_k$ is an array of items, then inserting $x_1, \dots, x_k$ into $T$ one at a time, in this order, gives a table whose contents are the contents of $T$ followed by $x_1, \dots, x_k$.
nodes.title: Inserting an array appends it to the contents

nodes.summary: Starting from the empty dynamic table and inserting the items of an array of length $k$ one at a time, the resulting table has capacity (number of slots) at most $2k$.
nodes.title: Capacity after inserting into the empty table

nodes.summary: Starting from the empty dynamic table and inserting the items of an array of length $k$ one at a time, the total cost is at most $3k$, where each insertion costs one unit for writing the new item plus one unit for each old slot copied when a full table is doubled.
nodes.title: Total cost of insertions into the empty table

nodes.summary: Starting from the empty dynamic table and inserting the items of a nonempty array of length $k$ one at a time, the total cost is less than $3k$.
nodes.title: Strict cost bound for nonempty insertion sequences

nodes.summary: Call a dynamic table with item count $n$ well formed when, for every slot index $i$, slot $i$ is occupied exactly when $i < n$. If a dynamic table $T$ is well formed, then for every array $xs$, the table obtained from $T$ by inserting the entries of $xs$ one at a time with TABLE-INSERT, in array order, is again well formed.
nodes.title: Repeated insertion preserves well-formedness of a dynamic table

nodes.summary: Given a dynamic table $T$ and an array $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of items, the result of inserting the array into $T$ is obtained by starting from $T$ and inserting $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{k-1}$ one at a time with TABLE-INSERT, in array order. Its cost is the sum of the costs of the $k$ insertions; for an empty array the result is $T$ at cost $0$.
nodes.title: Inserting an array of items into a dynamic table

nodes.summary: For every dynamic table $T$ with item count $n$ and every item $x$, the table returned by inserting $x$ into $T$ with TABLE-INSERT has item count $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Insertion increases the item count by one

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with item count $n$ and capacity (number of slots) $m$, and let $x$ be an item. The table returned by inserting $x$ into $T$ with TABLE-INSERT has capacity $1$ if $m = 0$, capacity $2m$ if $m > 0$ and $n = m$, and capacity $m$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Capacity after an insertion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a well-formed dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$ and item count $n$, let $x$ be an item, and let $T'$ be the table returned by inserting $x$ into $T$ with TABLE-INSERT, with capacity $m'$. Then the slots of $T'$ are $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1}$, followed by a slot holding $x$, followed by $m' - (n + 1)$ empty slots.
nodes.title: Slots after an insertion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with item count $n$ and capacity $m$, and let $x$ be an item. Inserting $x$ into $T$ with TABLE-INSERT costs $1 + n$ if $m > 0$ and $n = m$, and costs $1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Cost of an insertion

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a well-formed dynamic table and $x$ is an item, then the table returned by inserting $x$ into $T$ with TABLE-INSERT is well formed.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves well-formedness

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$ and item count $n \le m$, and let $x$ be an item. Inserting $x$ into $T$ proceeds as follows. If $m = 0$, first replace the slots by a single empty slot. Then, if the table is full, that is, $n$ equals the current capacity $c$, allocate $2c$ empty slots and copy the $c$ old slots into the first $c$ of them, at cost $1$ per copied slot. Finally write $x$…
nodes.title: TABLE-INSERT

nodes.summary: A dynamic table with items of type $\alpha$ consists of an array of slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$, each either empty or holding an item of type $\alpha$, together with an item count $n$ satisfying $n \le m$. The number $m$ of slots is the capacity of the table.
nodes.title: Dynamic table

nodes.summary: A dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$ and item count $n$ is well formed if and only if, for every $i < m$, slot $s_i$ is occupied exactly when $i < n$.
nodes.title: Characterization of well-formed dynamic tables

nodes.summary: A dynamic table with slots $s_0, \dots, s_{m-1}$ and item count $n$ is well formed when, for every $i < m$, slot $s_i$ is occupied if and only if $i < n$; that is, the occupied slots are exactly the first $n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed dynamic table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
